newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Majority of Austrians unhappy with EU - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Austrians unhappy with EU - poll.

text.p: Austrian dissatisfaction with the European Union is running at an all-time high at 64 percent, a survey showed on Monday, and only 34 percent of those polled saw more advantages from EU membership.

Asked how they would vote were there a vote next Sunday, 62 percent of those polled said they would oppose EU membership while 36 percent would vote in favour, the survey conducted by the Austrian research institute Market said.
Of the 1,016 people questioned, two percent were undecided.
Austria joined the EU and its exchange rate mechanism in January 1995 after more than two-thirds of Austrians voted in favour of membership in a referendum in June 1994.

The Market survey, conducted in April, showed that every second Austrian is against the single currency and that approval for the euro fell to 21 percent from 27 percent a year ago. Some 28 percent had no opinion.
According to the research institute, EU euphoria stood at a high in July 1994 with 60 percent approval, and disapproval was lowest in October 1994 at 36 percent.
